tutorial.welcomeBody: Make yourself at home: build your furniture pieces one by one, arrange them in a 3D room and, when you like the result, send them straight into a request. Take the short mission tour — two minutes and you'll know everything the studio can do.

createPiece.title: Your first piece
createPiece.body: Press “New piece” in the left panel, pick a body type and shape it with the sliders. When you save, the piece lands right in the room.

orbit.title: Take a walk around it
orbit.body: Hold the mouse down on an empty part of the room and move it to turn the view around; scroll to zoom in and out.

movePiece.title: Put it in its place
movePiece.body: Grab the piece and drag it across the floor. For precision: arrow keys move it 1 cm (Shift = 5), and in the floating panel you can type the exact distance to each wall.

rotatePiece.title: Face it the right way
rotatePiece.body: Select the piece with a click, then press R — or the rotate button in the floating panel.

addOpening.title: Cut a door or a window
addOpening.body: In the bar under the room, click a door, window or outlet to put it on a wall — or drag it straight onto the wall you want.

adjustOpening.title: Fit it to the wall
adjustOpening.body: With the opening selected, slide it along the wall or adjust its dimensions in the panel. R moves it to the next wall.

styleRoom.title: Make the room yours
styleRoom.body: Same bottom bar: set the room's width and depth to the centimetre and pick the wall and floor colours.

addScene.title: One more room
addScene.body: A project can hold several rooms. Press “New room” above the scene — then hop between them from the tabs, each with its own pieces.

undo.title: No regrets
undo.body: Broke something? Ctrl+Z steps back, Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes. Try one step back right now.
undo.hint: Nothing to undo yet — make a small change first (nudge the piece with an arrow key), then press Ctrl+Z.

tutorial.finaleBody: You've covered everything that matters. A few things worth knowing before you go:
tutorial.finaleTip1: “My drafts” saves the project to your account — pick it up again anytime.
tutorial.finaleTip2: F = fullscreen, and the floating panel moves by its grip, wherever you like it.
tutorial.finaleTip3: “Add to request” sends the whole room into the form — companies see exactly what you built.
tutorial.finaleReplay: Replay the tour anytime from the “?” button above the room.

SketchGuidePage.title: How to sketch your space
SketchGuidePage.subtitle: No architect needed — four simple steps give the companies everything they need to quote accurately. The sheet on the left shows exactly what your sketch needs to include.
SketchGuidePage.legendWall: The wall, measured corner to corner — width and height
SketchGuidePage.legendSocket: Sockets and pipes, marked with ✕ or a dashed circle
SketchGuidePage.legendFurniture: The furniture you want, drawn simply over the wall
SketchGuidePage.legendDimensions: The furniture dimensions, noted right on the drawing

measure.title: Measure the walls
measure.body: Take the length of every wall and the ceiling height. Measure at floor level, corner to corner.
measure.tip: A simple tape measure is enough — round to the centimetre.

draw.title: Draw the plan from above
draw.body: A simple rectangle is enough. Write each dimension right on its side, like in the example.
draw.tip: It doesn't have to be to scale — the numbers matter, not pretty drawing.

mark.title: Mark what can't move
mark.body: Doors with their swing, windows, sockets, pipes, radiators. Anything the future furniture could touch.
mark.tip: An ✕ for sockets, a double line for windows — like the socket mark on the sheet.

photo.title: Photograph and attach
photo.body: One clear photo, from above, with the whole sketch in frame. Attach it to your request along with photos of the room.
photo.tip: Natural light, no shadows over the numbers.

PAL.label: Chipboard (PAL)
PAL.description: Lowest price, wide choice of decors, sturdy

info.title: Melamine chipboard
info.body: Melamine-faced chipboard — the standard for cabinet carcasses, with the best price-to-durability ratio.
info.pros1: The best price per linear metre — your budget goes to fittings instead
info.pros2: Hundreds of decors: plain colours, wood grains, even concrete looks
info.pros3: The melamine surface shrugs off everyday scratches
info.cons1: Edges need ABS banding, or they show and wear
info.cons2: Swells if water reaches an unsealed cut

MDF.label: MDF
MDF.description: Painted or foil-wrapped fronts, refined look

info.title: Painted/foiled MDF
info.body: Medium-density fibreboard — the right base for painted, routed or foil-wrapped fronts.
info.pros1: Smooth surface — paint goes on evenly, with no board texture
info.pros2: Can be routed: profiles, frames, classic patterns
info.pros3: Edges finish cleanly, no applied banding needed
info.cons1: Costs more than chipboard for the same piece
info.cons2: The boards are heavy — large units need matching hardware

MDF_INFOLIAT.label: Foil-wrapped MDF
MDF_INFOLIAT.description: PVC foil on routed fronts, easy to keep clean

info.title: Foil-wrapped MDF
info.body: MDF fronts wrapped in heat-pressed PVC foil — routed patterns and a clean look at a moderate price.
info.pros1: The foil keeps water out — works in kitchens and bathrooms
info.pros2: Wipes clean with a cloth, no special products needed
info.pros3: Allows routed fronts, with frames or classic patterns
info.cons1: Next to an oven or hob, the foil can peel over time
info.cons2: A narrower colour palette than painted MDF

MDF_VOPSIT.label: Painted MDF
MDF_VOPSIT.description: Any RAL colour, matte or gloss finish

info.title: Painted MDF
info.body: Electrostatically painted MDF fronts — any RAL colour, in matte, satin or gloss.
info.pros1: Any colour and sheen — matches the rest of your home exactly
info.pros2: Fine edges with no visible banding — the most refined look
info.pros3: A scratch can be repainted locally, no front replacement
info.cons1: Among the most expensive front options
info.cons2: Paint can chip on a direct knock

MDF_FURNIR.label: Veneered MDF
MDF_FURNIR.description: Natural wood veneer on a stable core

info.title: Veneered MDF
info.body: MDF wrapped in natural wood veneer — the authentic grain of wood, without solid timber's warping risk.
info.pros1: Real wood grain, there to see and to touch
info.pros2: The MDF core won't warp the way solid wood does
info.pros3: Can be stained to the shade you want, just like wood
info.cons1: Rare veneers cost close to solid wood
info.cons2: Deep scratches cut through the thin veneer layer

info.title: Solid wood
info.body: Solid natural timber — the most durable option, with a grain unique to every piece.
info.pros1: Lasts for decades and can always be repaired
info.pros2: Every piece has its own grain — no two are alike
info.pros3: Can be sanded and refinished to look new again
info.cons1: The most expensive material option
info.cons2: Moves with humidity — it can crack or warp

otherMaterial.subtitle: Briefly describe the material or finish you want — the company will confirm whether they can work with it.

pieceSystems.title: Which opening system?
pieceSystems.subtitle: For this piece's doors and drawers — you can pick several.

info.title: Push-to-open
info.body: Fronts open with a light press, no handles — the line stays completely clean.
info.pros1: Smooth fronts with no handle to break the line
info.pros2: Opens with an elbow when your hands are full
info.cons1: Fingerprints show quickly on smooth fronts
info.cons2: The mechanism needs adjusting more often than a classic hinge

info.title: Sliding systems
info.body: Sliding doors move sideways along tracks; drawers pull out on runners. Allow clearance in front of drawers.
info.pros1: Sliding doors do not swing into the room; allow space to stand and access the cabinet
info.pros2: Carries wide, heavy fronts, all the way to the ceiling
info.cons1: Good rails cost more — cheap ones you feel on every open
info.cons2: Needs precise fitting — a skewed rail is heard and felt

info.title: Press latch
info.body: A simple click mechanism — the most affordable handleless opening.
info.pros1: The smallest investment for handleless fronts
info.pros2: A simple mechanism — easy to fit and to replace
info.cons1: Wears out faster than quality push systems
info.cons2: The door shuts hard, with no soft-close

MANER.label: Handle
MANER.description: Mounted handles, model of your choice

info.title: Classic handles
info.body: Handles mounted on the fronts — from minimal to classic; you choose the model together with the company.
info.pros1: A sure grip that works the same after ten years
info.pros2: Thousands of models — handles alone can change the look
info.cons1: Always visible — they become part of the design
info.cons2: Can catch clothes as you pass in narrow spaces

GOLA.label: Gola
GOLA.description: Cabinet-mounted profile for a handleless grip

info.title: Gola profile
info.body: An aluminium channel set between the fronts — you open from the profile and the front line stays unbroken.
info.pros1: An unbroken line with no handles — the modern kitchen look
info.pros2: Nothing sticks out — nothing to catch as you pass by
info.cons1: Routing and the profile add to the price
info.cons2: Demanding to fit — a job for an experienced team

AVENTOS.label: Aventos (lift-up)
AVENTOS.description: The front lifts up, with soft-close

info.title: Aventos system
info.body: Wall-cabinet fronts lift on damped arms — full access, with no open door at head height.
info.pros1: No more open doors to bump into above the worktop
info.pros2: The front stays open at any position until you pull it down
info.cons1: The most expensive opening system
info.cons2: The arms need periodic adjustment to stay balanced

layout.title: What shape is the kitchen?
layout.subtitle: Pick the layout that fits your space.

info.title: Straight kitchen
info.body: All cabinets along one wall — compact, a natural fit for small spaces.
info.pros1: Lowest cost per metre of any layout
info.pros2: Fits narrow kitchens and open-plan living areas
info.pros3: Quick to install: one wall, no corners to solve
info.cons1: The worktop stays short — serious cooking takes organising
info.cons2: Less storage; tall units become almost essential

info.title: L-shaped kitchen
info.body: Cabinets on two walls — a good balance of worktop and circulation.
info.pros1: Sink, hob and fridge sit close — short paths while cooking
info.pros2: Fits most apartments without blocking the walkway
info.pros3: Leaves room for a table or a breakfast corner
info.cons1: The corner is hard to reach without dedicated fittings
info.cons2: Corner systems (carousel, pull-out) add to the price

info.title: U-shaped kitchen
info.body: Cabinets on three sides — maximum storage and worktop.
info.pros1: Storage on three sides — you'll rarely need another cupboard
info.pros2: Generous worktop: cook and prep in parallel
info.pros3: Separate zones for cooking, washing and prep
info.cons1: Feels cramped in rooms under 2.4 m wide
info.cons2: Two corners to solve — each needs fittings or wastes space

info.title: Galley kitchen
info.body: Two facing runs — efficient in pass-through kitchens.
info.pros1: Everything one step away — the layout cooks prefer
info.pros2: Two people can cook without getting in each other's way
info.cons1: The aisle between runs needs at least 1.2 m clear
info.cons2: No room left for a table in the kitchen

hasIsland.title: Do you want an island?
hasIsland.subtitle: An island adds worktop, storage and a place to eat.

info.title: Kitchen island
info.body: A freestanding unit in the middle — leave at least 1.2 m of clearance on every side.
info.pros1: Extra worktop and storage, right at the centre of the action
info.pros2: Doubles as a breakfast bar or a spot for guests
info.cons1: Only works in large kitchens — otherwise it blocks circulation
info.cons2: A separate unit and worktop — the cost adds up visibly

countertop.subtitle: Optional — helps the company estimate more accurately.

info.title: Laminated chipboard worktop
info.body: Chipboard core with a laminated surface — the affordable standard, hundreds of designs.
info.pros1: Lowest price — easy to replace years later without regrets
info.pros2: Hundreds of designs: wood, stone, plain colours
info.cons1: Edges swell if water gets past the sealing
info.cons2: Scratches and dulls visibly in heavy-use areas

info.title: HPL worktop
info.body: High-pressure laminate — far denser and tougher than standard chipboard.
info.pros1: Handles water, scratches and daily wear far better than chipboard
info.pros2: Can be slim, for a clean, modern line
info.cons1: Roughly double the price of a standard laminate top
info.cons2: Narrower range of designs than regular laminate

info.title: Laminate countertop
info.body: Laminated chipboard — the budget option with the widest choice of designs.
info.pros1: The lowest-priced worktop of all
info.pros2: Designs for any style, from wood to concrete
info.cons1: Deep scratches cannot be repaired
info.cons2: Hot pans straight on the top leave marks — use a trivet

info.title: Quartz countertop
info.body: Engineered stone — among the most durable and hygienic worktops.
info.pros1: Nearly impossible to scratch in everyday use
info.pros2: Non-porous surface: doesn't stain, easy to keep hygienic
info.cons1: Among the priciest worktop options
info.cons2: Very heavy — cabinets must be built to carry it

info.title: Granite countertop
info.body: Natural stone — durable, with a unique pattern in every slab.
info.pros1: Natural stone that takes decades of daily use
info.pros2: Every slab has a one-of-a-kind pattern
info.cons1: Needs periodic sealing, or it can stain
info.cons2: High price, and so are transport and fitting

info.title: Wood countertop
info.body: Solid wood — a warm look, cared for with periodic oiling.
info.pros1: Warms up any kitchen — works in modern styles too
info.pros2: Scratches sand out; the top can be refinished any time
info.cons1: Needs regular oiling, especially around the sink
info.cons2: Standing water stains and swells the wood

info.title: Linear closet
info.body: Modules along a single wall — the compact option for a bedroom or hallway.
info.pros1: Takes up one wall — the rest of the room stays free
info.pros2: The lowest-cost configuration
info.cons1: Limited capacity — choose carefully what lives here

info.title: L-shaped closet
info.body: Modules on two walls — puts the corner to work.
info.pros1: Serious capacity without taking over the room
info.pros2: An otherwise wasted corner becomes storage
info.cons1: The corner stays awkward without dedicated modules

info.title: U-shaped closet
info.body: Modules on three sides — maximum storage capacity.
info.pros1: The most storage per square metre
info.pros2: Separate zones: hanging, drawers, shelves
info.cons1: Needs a generous room, or you'll be bumping into doors

info.title: Walk-in closet
info.body: A dedicated room, with modules on several walls.
info.pros1: Your whole wardrobe visible, in one place
info.pros2: Get dressed on the spot, no doors to open
info.cons1: You give up a room, or part of one

info.title: Sliding doors
info.body: Doors that glide on rails — they need no swing space at all.
info.pros1: Sit flush against a bed or wall — zero swing space
info.pros2: One large, continuous surface — great for mirrors too
info.cons1: Good rails cost more — cheap ones wear out fast

info.title: Hinged doors
info.body: Classic hinged doors — full access to the interior.
info.pros1: Open a door and see the whole interior at a glance
info.pros2: Hinges cost less than any sliding system
info.cons1: Open doors need clear space in front of the wardrobe

info.title: Open closet
info.body: Doorless modules — everything visible and within reach.
info.pros1: Grab what you need in a single motion
info.pros2: No doors, no hardware — the lowest cost
info.cons1: Dust settles on clothes — takes constant tidiness

info.title: Hanging rods
info.body: The classic hanger zone. One metre of rod holds about 10–12 hangers; long dresses need 150–160 cm of free height.

info.title: Drawers
info.body: The priciest interior module: slides, fronts, assembly. Soft-close is worth it in daily-use zones.

info.title: Shelves
info.body: The most affordable modules. Adjustable shelves cost a little extra and pay off quickly.

info.title: Shoe rack
info.body: Tilted shelves with a stopper or pull-out racks. Allow about 20 cm of width per pair.

info.title: Interior accessories
info.body: Pull-out trouser rack, belt and tie holders, wire baskets. They can be added later, but come out cheaper planned from the start.

info.title: LED lighting
info.body: LED strip under the shelves or along the sides, usually with a door or motion sensor. Needs power — tell the company where the closest outlet is.

info.title: Floor-to-ceiling closet
info.body: Modules run all the way up: no dust collecting on top, and you gain room for seasonal items. Ceilings are rarely perfectly level — careful measuring required.
info.pros1: Nothing gathers dust above the wardrobe
info.pros2: The top zone holds bedding and out-of-season clothes
info.cons1: You'll need a step stool for the top shelves

lighting.title: Integrated LED lighting?
lighting.subtitle: LED strip with a door sensor.

info.title: LED lighting
info.body: LED strip under the shelves or along the sides, usually with a door or motion sensor. Needs power — tell the company where the closest outlet is.
info.pros1: See the whole interior, even at night
info.pros2: Warm light gives the interior a premium feel
info.cons1: Needs a power outlet nearby

info.title: Sliding doors
info.body: Doors glide on tracks, one passing in front of the other — the natural choice when the bed sits close to the wardrobe.

info.pros2: Large panels, clean front — flatters wide wardrobes

info.title: Hinged doors
info.body: Classic doors on hinges — open both and see the whole interior at a glance. They need about 50 cm of clearance in front.
info.pros1: Full access: the whole interior visible at once
info.pros2: The most affordable option, with easy-to-adjust hinges
info.cons1: Each door needs ~50 cm of clearance in front

info.title: Floor-to-ceiling wardrobe
info.body: The unit goes all the way up, with no dead space above. Height is measured in several spots — ceilings are rarely perfectly level.
info.pros1: No more dust collecting on top of the wardrobe
info.pros2: Top shelves take suitcases and seasonal items
info.cons1: You only reach the top shelves with a step stool

info.body: Common sizes in Romania: 90×200 (single), 140×200 (compact double), 160×200 (the standard double), 180×200 (king). Note: the mattress is not included.

info.title: Simple bed
info.body: A classic frame with no mechanisms — the lowest price and the easiest to move when needed.

info.title: Gas-lift base with storage box
info.body: The mattress lifts on gas pistons, revealing a storage box the full size of the bed — the largest hidden storage in the bedroom.

info.title: Under-bed drawers
info.body: Two to four drawers that pull out sideways, no need to lift the mattress. They need clear floor space beside the bed to open.

info.title: Upholstered bed
info.body: Frame and headboard wrapped in fabric or eco-leather — soft to the touch, with plenty of colours to pick from. You choose the exact fabric together with the company.

info.title: One or a pair
info.body: A pair costs nearly double, but visually balances a double bed. For a single bed, one is enough.

info.title: Floating TV unit
info.body: A horizontal unit fixed to the wall — the floor stays completely clear, and the room feels bigger.
info.pros1: The room feels more spacious — the whole floor stays visible
info.pros2: Vacuum and mop under it without moving a thing
info.cons1: Needs a solid wall; plasterboard requires reinforcement

ON_FLOOR.description: Unit standing on legs or a plinth

info.title: Floor-standing TV unit
info.body: The classic choice that always works: storage for electronics and media, with the TV on top or wall-mounted above.
info.pros1: The lowest price of the three options
info.pros2: Move it any time, with no holes or marks on the wall
info.cons1: A single unit — storage stops at what fits inside it

info.title: TV unit with cabinets
info.body: A full-wall composition: TV unit with cabinets or columns on the sides, often with a niche and LED lighting.
info.pros1: The most storage, hidden behind the fronts
info.pros2: The wall reads as one design, not furnished piece by piece
info.cons1: The biggest investment, and installation is a project in itself

intro.h: 1. Who we are and what Cozy Home is
intro.b:
The Cozy Home platform (the “Platform”) is operated by {operator} (the “Operator”, “we”).

Cozy Home is a marketplace connecting people who want custom furniture (“Clients”) with partner furniture companies (“Companies”). The Platform facilitates publishing requests, claiming them, messaging and sending offers; the furniture contract is concluded directly between the Client and the Company, and the Operator is not a party to it.

accounts.h: 2. Accounts and use of the Platform
accounts.b:
An account is required to publish a request or send offers. You are responsible for keeping your credentials confidential and for all activity in your account.

You agree to provide accurate information, not to publish unlawful, misleading or offensive content, and not to use the Platform against its purpose (for example harvesting other users' data or unsolicited advertising). We may suspend or close accounts that breach these terms.

The Operator may block an account that breaches these terms. Blocking immediately revokes active sessions, and the user is notified by email.

flow.b:
The Client publishes a request with project details; a limited number of Companies can claim it and send offers. The Client's contact details become visible only to Companies that claimed the request.

Offers are commercial proposals of the Companies. Prices, deadlines, warranties and any other conditions belong exclusively to the issuing Company. Budget estimates shown by the Platform are indicative and do not constitute offers.

delivery.h: 4. Delivery and completion of the request
delivery.b:
The Company marks the order as delivered in the Platform, and the Client confirms delivery. If the Client neither confirms nor reports a problem within 14 calendar days of the delivery being marked, the request is automatically marked as completed.

Upon completion, the winning Company's reserved credits are consumed, leaving a review becomes possible, and the Client and the Company are notified.

reviews.b:
The Client can leave a review for a request only after it is completed, once per request. A review under 3 stars automatically opens a dispute, handled by the Platform administrator, who joins a conversation only in disputes.

If the dispute is resolved, the review stays on record. If the dispute is dismissed, the review is deleted and the Client may leave a new one. The Platform's mediation does not replace the contract between the Client and the Company.

credits.b:
Companies access requests based on a subscription and credits. Credits spent claiming a request are not refunded except in the cases explicitly covered by the Platform rules (for example the Client cancelling the request, or withdrawals under accepted conditions).

Pricing and packages are shown in the Platform and may change; changes do not affect credits already purchased.

penalties.b:
Companies receive penalty points for: an expired offer or a missed response deadline (3 points); all Companies that claimed a request missing the response deadline (3 points each); voluntarily withdrawing a claim without a reason after the 30-minute grace period (2 points). Each point expires 180 days after it is applied.

A Company that reaches the current threshold (12 active points) is suspended for the current period (6 months) and cannot claim new requests. The points and thresholds may be updated by the Operator; the values in force are those shown in the Platform.

liability.b:
The Operator makes reasonable efforts to keep the Platform running but does not guarantee error-free or uninterrupted availability.

The Operator is not liable for the execution, quality, delivery or warranty of furniture contracted between Client and Company, nor for user-generated content. Disputes between Client and Company are resolved between them; the Platform may mediate within its existing dispute features.

ip.b:
The Platform, the Cozy Home brand, its design and own content are protected by intellectual property rights and may not be used without our written consent.

By uploading content (photos, sketches, descriptions), users grant the Operator a non-exclusive licence to display it in the Platform for the purpose of running the service. Companies warrant they hold the necessary rights over portfolio photos.

changes.b:
We may update these terms to reflect legal or functional changes. The current version is always published on this page.

For significant changes we will ask you to accept the updated terms again the next time you use the Platform; until then, some features may be unavailable.

law.b:

For any questions about these terms write to {contactEmail}.

intro.b:
Your personal data is processed by {operator} (the “Controller”), in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR).

You can contact us about anything related to data protection at {contactEmail}.

data.h: 2. What data we collect and why
data.b:
We collect and store the following categories of data:

• Account data: name, email address, phone number (optional), password (stored encrypted), language preference — to create and manage your account.
• Request data: project description, delivery/installation address, city and county, chosen contact channels (email, phone) — to publish the request and, once claimed, to share with the Companies working on it.
• Company data: company name, tax ID, addresses, team — to verify and display the company in the Platform.
• The content of conversations held in the Platform (stored encrypted) and uploaded files — to run messaging and offers.
• Uploaded photos are automatically cleaned of hidden data (such as the GPS location stored in the photo) before Companies see them; PDF and ZIP files stay as you uploaded them.
• Technical and usage data: IP address, device type, pages visited and actions performed in the Platform.
• The version of the Terms and Privacy Policy you accepted and the moment you accepted them.

The address field in the configurator may load the Google Maps Places script (Google LLC) to suggest addresses — only when the Platform has such an integration enabled. At that moment your IP address and the text typed into the field reach Google, under Google's privacy policy.

To turn the delivery address or a company's address into coordinates, our servers send the address text, city and county (without name or contact details) to the Nominatim service of the OpenStreetMap Foundation (United Kingdom).

The legal bases are contract performance (providing the service), legitimate interest (security and improving the Platform) and, where required by law, your consent.

usage.b: We analyse how the Platform is used (pages visited, features used, errors encountered) to understand what works and what needs improvement. These analyses use aggregated or pseudonymised data wherever possible and are not aimed at building individual profiles for purposes other than product improvement and service security.

marketing.b:
With your consent, we may send you commercial communications about the Platform (news, features, offers) and may use usage data for more relevant marketing and advertising campaigns.

You can withdraw your consent at any time, with immediate effect: via the unsubscribe link present in every email, or by writing to {contactEmail}. Withdrawing consent does not affect your normal use of the Platform.

sharing.b:
While your request is published for Companies, verified Companies whose coverage area includes your locality see the project: title, description, rooms, uploaded files, 3D scene, city, county and an approximate distance. Phone numbers, email addresses and links written in texts are hidden from them.

Your name, full address and chosen contact channels (always including your account email) are shared only with Companies that claimed the request, while their claim is active or the project is carried out with them, so they can contact you and send offers. Access ends when the Company withdraws its claim or you accept another Company's offer. The request page shows which Companies hold them.

We use the following providers, which process data on our behalf under GDPR-compliant contracts:

• Railway Corporation (USA) — hosting of the application, database, file storage and processing queues.
• Stripe (Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd., Ireland, and its affiliates including Stripe, Inc., USA) — online payments by Companies for credits and subscriptions (email address and company identifier).
• Our transactional email provider — account emails and notifications.
• Google LLC (Google Maps Places) — address suggestions, only when the integration is active.
• OpenStreetMap Foundation (Nominatim) — turning addresses into coordinates.
• Our error-monitoring provider (hosted in the EU) — technical reports about errors in the Platform (error type, page, app version), without form contents, email addresses or cookies; only when the integration is active.
• Our cookieless usage-statistics provider (hosted in the EU) — counts of requests started and published, without identifying you; only when the integration is active.

We do not sell your personal data to third parties.

transfers.h: 6. Transfers outside the European Economic Area
transfers.b:
Some of the providers above (Railway, Stripe, Google) are based in the USA, and some servers may be located outside the European Economic Area.

Transfers rely on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses (Article 46(2)(c) GDPR) and/or, for certified providers, on the adequacy decision for the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. The United Kingdom benefits from a European Commission adequacy decision. You can request a copy of the safeguards applied at {contactEmail}.

rights.b:
You have the right of access to your data, the right to rectification, the right to erasure (“right to be forgotten”), the right to restrict processing, the right to data portability, the right to object (including to marketing) and the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing.

To exercise these rights, write to {contactEmail}; we reply within one month at the latest. If you consider that the processing breaches the law, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Romanian supervisory authority (ANSPDCP, www.dataprotection.ro).

retention.b:
We keep account data for as long as the account is active. Upon your account deletion request (sent to {contactEmail}), personal data is deleted or anonymised within a reasonable period, except for data we are legally required to keep (for example accounting records) and data strictly necessary to defend legal claims.

Technical usage data is kept for limited periods, proportionate to the purpose it was collected for.

cookies.b:
The Platform uses strictly necessary cookies: session authentication (httpOnly cookies) and remembering your chosen language (RO/EN).

We currently use no third-party advertising cookies. If we introduce non-essential cookies (for example for analytics or marketing), we will ask for your consent beforehand and update this section.

firmRules.title: Rules for firms
firmRules.intro: These rules detail sections 6 and 7 of the <terms>Terms and Conditions</terms> and describe exactly what the Platform applies today. The values (deadlines, points, thresholds) are the ones in force right now and update automatically on this page.

verification.b:
After you submit your firm details (name, CUI, address), the firm goes into verification. Until it is approved you cannot see or claim requests.

If the verification request is rejected, a new application with the same CUI or the same firm administrator email is possible only {reapplyMonths} after the rejection.

trial.b: When your firm is approved you get the {plan} subscription free for {durationDays} and {bonusCredits} as a bonus.
trial.bOff: No trial period is currently granted when a firm is approved.

credits.b:
To see and claim requests you need an active subscription. The credit cost of each claim is shown on the request before you claim it and stays the one from the moment you claim. When you claim, the credits are reserved, not yet consumed. A request can be claimed by at most {maxClaims} firms.

After claiming, the request must be assigned to a team member within {assignMinutes}; otherwise the claim is cancelled automatically and the reserved credits are refunded.
credits.afterOfferClosed: Once one of the firms that claimed the request sends the first offer, no other firm can claim it, even if not all {maxClaims} places are taken.
credits.afterOfferOpen: The request stays open for claiming after the first offer, until {maxClaims} firms have claimed it or the client accepts an offer. Your response deadline runs from the moment you claim.
credits.costRange: A claim costs at least {min} and at most {max}.

settlement.h: 4. When credits are consumed and when they are refunded
settlement.b:
• Your offer is accepted: the credits are consumed when the project is completed, that is when the client confirms delivery or automatically, {autoCompleteDays} after you mark the delivery.
• You sent an offer, but the client chose another firm: the credits are consumed (you pay for the chance to bid).
• You claimed the request but had not yet sent an offer when the client accepts another firm offer: the credits are refunded.
• The client deletes the request: the credits are refunded.
• You do not send the offer within the response deadline: the credits are consumed (section 5).
• You withdraw from the claim: see section 6.
• The project is cancelled by the administrator after acceptance: the administrator decides, with a written note, whether the credits are refunded or consumed.

sla.b:
After claiming you have a deadline to send the offer: {small} for small projects, {medium} for medium ones and {large} for large ones. Working days exclude weekends and public holidays. The exact deadline appears on the claim work sheet.

A clarification question sent to the client pauses the deadline until they answer and extends it by {clarificationDays}.

If you do not send the offer by the deadline plus {graceHours} of grace, the claim expires, the reserved credits are consumed and the firm receives {slaMissPoints} of penalty. If the request then returns to the marketplace, the firms that missed the deadline on it can no longer claim it.

withdrawals.b:
The firm owner and managers can withdraw an open claim at any time; other members can withdraw only their own claim, within the first {graceMinutes}. Once the client accepts an offer, the claim can no longer be withdrawn.

• Voluntary withdrawal within the first {graceMinutes}: the credits are fully refunded, with no penalty.
• Voluntary withdrawal after {graceMinutes}: the credits are consumed, the slot is freed for other firms and the firm receives {withdrawalPoints} of penalty.
• You messaged the client in the app (a message or a clarification question) and they have not replied for {unresponsiveHours}: the withdrawal is approved automatically and your credits are refunded.
• The request was changed after you claimed it and you have not sent an offer since the change: the withdrawal is approved automatically and your credits are refunded.
• Invalid contact details, cancellation requested by the client or another reason: the withdrawal is reviewed by the administrator, and until the decision the slot stays occupied. If approved, the credits are refunded; if rejected, the claim continues.
withdrawals.contactsOnClaim: The client's contact details and full address are visible to your firm right after the claim, for as long as the claim is active. Employees with a limited role see them only on their own claims.
withdrawals.contactsAfterGrace: The client's contact details and full address become visible {graceMinutes} after the claim, for as long as the claim is active. Employees with a limited role see them only on their own claims.
withdrawals.contactsRetention: {days} after delivery, the contact details of completed projects stay visible only to the firm's owner and managers.

penalties.b: The firm receives penalty points only for:

items.SLA_MISS: offer not sent within the response deadline: {points}
items.VOLUNTARY_WITHDRAWAL: voluntary withdrawal after the grace period: {points}

penalties.after: Each penalty expires separately, {windowDays} after it is applied. Active points and the expiry date of each are shown in the wallet.

suspension.b: When the firm reaches {threshold} active, it is suspended for {months}. While suspended, the firm cannot see or claim requests and has no access to the firm work features; it can still see its points and the date the suspension ends. The suspension ends automatically on the date shown, and the firm is notified.

changes.b: The operator may change the values above; this page always shows the values in force. The cost and deadline of a claim already made stay the ones from the moment of the claim. If you have questions you can write to us at {contactEmail}.
